ai.title: Baseten Releases Bison-1 and Groundhog-1, Topping Decision Model Index
ai.brief: Baseten has released bison-1 and groundhog-1, 2 open-weight decision models built on Google’s Gemma 4 . Decision models do not write text. They return calibrated probabilities for yes/no, choice and score questions. 1 . That ranks #1 of 19. Both models raise context from 16k to 128k tokens and accept images. For routing, triage and guardrail pipelines, that means full policies and histories in one call. TL;DR Size: bison-1 is 31B dense. groundhog-1 is a 26B MoE with about 4B active. Both take 128k tokens (131,072). Runs on: Baseten Model APIs, plus open BF16 weights on Hugging Face. No inference GPU or quantized builds are listed. BF16 weights alone are about 62 GB (bison-1) and 52 GB (groundhog-1), by our arithmetic. 2-ultra (75). Best: When2Call, 98 (rank #1). 1, 60 (rank #11). 10 per 1M input tokens. Worst: groundhog-1 has no official index score yet, and every number is self-reported.
